text: TextIn xParse 是面向 DSH Web 的文档解析插件。它注册 xparse 工具和 xparse-parse 技能，并在插件设置与对话界面提供凭据配置和 OAuth 登录。用户可解析文档、查看配额、搜索和阅读内容，也可提交并管理多文档任务。网络操作需要 TextIn Device OAuth 或成对配置的 App ID 与 Secret Code；文档解析会将文档数据发送给 TextIn。

TextIn xParse adds document parsing to DSH Web with an xparse tool and bundled skill. It parses files, searches content, checks quota, and manages multi-document tasks. Parsing sends document data to TextIn; network use requires Device OAuth or an App ID and Secret Code.
想让 DSH 帮我解析文档并查找里面的内容
怎么在 DSH 里查看文档解析任务的进度和结果？
I want to search and read content from parsed documents in DSH.
TextIn xParse 的功能「解析与检索文档」：通过 xparse 工具解析支持的文档，并查看解析内容、目录或搜索文本；工具操作由 DSH 调用并返回结果或产物路径。
TextIn xParse 的功能「多文档任务管理」：通过 xparse 工具提交或重跑文档任务，并查询任务状态、读取结果和导出任务产物。
TextIn xParse 使用解析或任务提交功能时会将文档数据发送给 TextIn 服务；工具描述明确说明了该数据流向。
TextIn xParse 的网络操作需要 Device OAuth 或完整的 AppKey；AppKey 由 XPARSE_APP_ID 与 XPARSE_SECRET_CODE 两个凭据引用组成。

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · TextIn xParse for DeepSeek Harness：English | [简体中文](README_zh.md)

`@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse` installs one structured `xparse` Tool, the bundled
`xparse-parse` Skill, and the reviewed xparse CLI binaries used internally by
the Tool.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or `0.2.1-rc.3`
- Node.js 22.19 or newer, as required by the current Harness dependency set
- Linux or macOS on x64/arm64; Windows binaries are packaged but are not part
  of the current native validation evidence

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse
dsh --profile web --dump-config
dsh --profile web
```

The Tool always executes the binary embedded in this package. It does not use
`PATH`, a global `xparse-cli`, an install script, or a runtime download.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Operations：The first release exposes:

- `parse`
- `quota`
- `get_doc_info`
- `get_outline`
- `search_text`
- `read_pages`
- `read_content`
- `task_run`
- `task_rerun`
- `task_status`
- `task_read`
- `task_export`
- `task_debug`
- `task_resume`

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Operations：`get_confidence`, interactive CLI commands, arbitrary CLI arguments, custom
headers, custom base URLs, Task passwords, `task_continue`, foreground Task
waiting controls, `task_status.details`, and encrypted-document passwords are
not exposed. Task submission and rerun operations return Task/Run identity,
status, progress counters, terminal state, and `next_action` immediately; use
the compact exact-Run `task_status` response for later progress checks. Task
debug/export responses expose only whitelisted file status, error code, and
recovery fields rather than raw service payloads.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Operations：Parsing sends document data to TextIn. Uploads and explicit paid parsing follow
the Bundle's Harness approval policy. Task auto-routing and reruns are not
pre-approved merely because they may later need paid capacity: the service
first returns `waiting_paid_authorization` or `waiting_funds`, and approval is
requested only for the exact subsequent `task_resume` action. One approval
covers that Task Run, not one approval per file; an `after-funding` retry for
the already-authorized Run does not ask again. Results are written as workspace
artifacts instead of returning a complete long document as Tool text.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Credentials：The browser card at **Plugins > TextIn xParse** writes App ID and Secret Code through the Harness
`credentials.set` API. Secret Code never enters plugin settings, Tool
arguments, or the Agent conversation. The card addresses the configured credential
references, which default to `XPARSE_APP_ID` and `XPARSE_SECRET_CODE`.
Credential references are projected through DSH's native `configForms` service.
The non-secret App ID and temporary OAuth CSRF token are read on demand through
an authenticated owner-only endpoint; they are not persisted as plugin settings.
Secret Code remains write-only. A
configured card shows App ID and a Modify action, while an unconfigured card
keeps the AppKey form collapsed until the user selects the AppKey configuration
button. The same nested control hides the configured App ID and modification
actions by default. The outer xParse card starts collapsed whenever OAuth is
already logged in or a complete AppKey exists; otherwise it starts expanded.
Deployment-provided environment values remain higher priority and make the
corresponding controls read-only. The same card offers Device OAuth login: the
Host automatic

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Credentials：OAuth access tokens enter the refresh window five minutes before expiry by
default (`oauthRefreshSkewMs: 300000`).

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Credentials：When a root Agent calls a network operation without usable credentials, the
Tool starts Device OAuth and opens a dedicated xParse login card in the
conversation composer. The card uses an aligned header, authorization panel,
and action footer for the xParse label, login requirement, verification link,
user code, and completion controls; it does not expose the generic question
form, skip, or submit controls. Successful authorization
closes the card, stores the grant Host-side, and continues the original Tool
call. The user may also confirm completion or cancel from the card. Login
waiting occurs before the CLI execution deadline.
Subagents, headless callers, and deployments without a question provider must
use the plugin settings card instead.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Credentials：Never paste App IDs, Secret Codes, OAuth tokens, or document passwords into a
conversation or Tool call.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · State and artifacts：The adapter assigns a session-scoped state directory below
`<workspace>/.xparse/sessions/` through `XPARSE_STATE_DIR`. Parse artifacts use
per-call directories below `<workspace>/.xparse/calls/`. The sandbox remains
the authority for file access. Every embedded CLI subprocess also receives
`XPARSE_CLIENT_FROM=deepseek-harness`, so TextIn API requests carry
`X-From: deepseek-harness` instead of the standalone `cli` attribution.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：This repository owns only the DeepSeek Harness plugin. The embedded CLI is
built by `xparse-client`, and the generic Skill is maintained by
`xparse-skills`; reviewed revisions are pinned in `release-lock.json` and
materialized only during assembly.

Install dependencies and run the source-level checks with:

```sh
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：Generated release inputs are intentionally not committed. CLI binaries are
downloaded from the six npm platform-package tarballs pinned by URL, npm
integrity, tarball SHA-256, and binary SHA-256 in `release-lock.json`. Populate
or verify the cache with:

```sh
npm run fetch:cli
npm run fetch:skill
```

Then assemble with a clean checkout of the locked Skill:

```sh
python3 scripts/prepare-dsh-xparse.py \
  --skill-dir /path/to/xparse-skills/skills/xparse-parse
```

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：Use `--offline` to prove the assembly is reproducible from the verified cache
without registry access.

After assembly, validate the package and a real DSH web boot with:

```sh
npm run validate:docker
```

Docker validation uses the public `node:22.22.0-bookworm` image, including Node
and Python. Set `DSH_VALIDATION_IMAGE` to override it.

Validate each supported Host version independently:

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：```sh
DSH_VALIDATION_DSH_VERSION=0.2.1-rc.2 npm run validate:docker
DSH_VALIDATION_DSH_VERSION=0.2.1-rc.3 npm run validate:docker
```

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：The script uses separate versioned Host caches and checks types against the
installed Host's actual packages. It verifies configuration projection, anonymous
access rejection, live credential-reference updates, App ID refresh and clearing,
OAuth CSRF checks, and the advertised browser bundle. To also exercise the settings
card in an existing temporary headless Chrome, supply its DevTools browser WebSocket
as `DSH_VALIDATION_BROWSER_WS` and use `DSH_VALIDATION_NETWORK=host` on Linux.
The browser check saves, edits, updates, and clears test AppKeys; it stubs OAuth
status in the browser and does not authorize against TextIn.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：Check the tag and supported platforms, then pull and smoke-test the image before
running validation:

```sh
docker manifest inspect node:22.22.0-bookworm
docker pull node:22.22.0-bookworm
docker run --rm node:22.22.0-bookworm bash -lc \
  'set -eu; node --version; npm --version; python3 --version; git --version'

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Development：A registry connection timeout does not establish whether a tag exists. Docker's
[official image record](https://github.com/docker-library/repo-info/blob/a41680605495ed0bba5495ed48e7caf405cf1c1f/repos/node/remote/22.22.0-bookworm.md)
records this tag and its platform digests; a successful pull and validation are
still required to establish that it works in your environment.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Release：Build the complete npm tarball and checksum manifest with one command:

```sh
npm run release:build -- --output-dir dist/release
```

The command fetches the locked Skill and CLI artifacts, assembles generated
inputs, compiles TypeScript, runs `npm pack`, verifies the tarball, and writes
`SHA256SUMS`. Add `--offline` to require both verified caches.

Before publication, run the same content audit enforced by the release workflow:

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Release：The release workflow intentionally skips the six locked CLI binaries because the
upstream CLI path-leak exception is currently accepted. It still checks every
other archive member for internal infrastructure, non-production API URLs,
developer home paths, and employee emails. Run without `--skip-cli-binaries`
when reviewing a new upstream CLI build. This targeted audit does not replace
credential scanning or an upstream environment access review.

@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse README · Release：GitHub CI performs the same release build on every pull request and uploads the
review artifact. Pushing tag `v<package-version>` runs the release workflow,
publishes the exact verified tarball to npm, and attaches the tarball plus
checksums to a GitHub Release. Configure repository secret `NPM_TOKEN` with
publish access to `@intsig-xparse/dsh-xparse` before creating a release tag.
